background_notes.justification: This is a routine ordered-field endpoint completion of the stated supremum argument, not an additional dimension theorem. D is an upper bound. Given real r<D, put m=max(0,r) and s=(m+D)/2; then 0<s<D and r<s. For the shifted conclusion, Q=∞ is immediate. If Q<D+1, it has a finite real value q≥0. Now m=max(0,q-1)<D and s=(m+D)/2 satisfies 0<s<D and s+1>q, contradicting the available lower bound Q≥s+1. These explicit midpoint inequalities require only elementary arithmetic and order; there is no limit exchange or extra hypothesis.
